title: Support wants to “see the problem”
scenario: A caller claiming to be from your bank says malware may be causing suspicious transfers. They ask you to install a remote-support app so they can inspect your phone while you log in.

answers.A: Do not install the app; end the call and contact the bank through its official channel, then secure the device separately if needed.
answers.B: Use the bank app to freeze transactions first and ask a trusted tech-support provider to inspect the device.
answers.C: Install the app but close your banking app before giving them screen access.

explanation: Remote-control tools can expose passwords, messages and approvals even if the banking app is closed.
proTip: If the helper needs control of your screen, verify the helper first.
